title: Executive Community Charter Template
instructions: Complete this with founding members before accepting sponsors or launching a recurring program.
content:
# [COMMUNITY NAME] Charter

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Owner: [NAME OR ROLE]

## Purpose
[COMMUNITY NAME] exists to help [MEMBER PROFILE] address [SHARED DECISIONS OR CHALLENGES] through [FORMATS].

## Membership
Members must [ROLE AND SCOPE CRITERIA]. Admission is decided by [DECISION OWNER]. Conflicts are reviewed using [PROCESS]. Membership may be reviewed when a member changes role.

## Participation
Members agree to prepare, contribute relevant experience, respect time, avoid hard pitching and follow the stated confidentiality rule.

## Confidentiality
Sessions use [CHATHAM HOUSE RULE / OFF-THE-RECORD RULE / CUSTOM RULE]. Recording and photography are [POLICY]. The community cannot promise legal privilege or absolute confidentiality.

## Sponsors
Sponsors may [RIGHTS]. Sponsors may not [RESTRICTIONS]. Participant data is handled according to [PRIVACY NOTICE].

## Conduct and removal
Concerns may be reported to [CONTACT]. The community may warn, pause or remove a member for [REASONS]. The decision and appeal process is [PROCESS].

## Review
This charter is reviewed every [PERIOD] by [OWNER]. Material changes are communicated before they take effect.

Disclaimer: Adapt this template to your community and obtain qualified legal or privacy advice where required.

title: Executive Community Invitation Email
instructions: Personalize the reason for invitation and remove any language that suggests automatic acceptance.
content:
# Member Invitation Email

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]

Subject: Invitation to [COMMUNITY OR SESSION NAME]

Hello [FIRST NAME],

I am inviting you to [COMMUNITY OR SESSION] because [SPECIFIC REASON CONNECTED TO ROLE OR EXPERIENCE].

The group brings together [MEMBER PROFILE] to discuss [DECISIONS OR TOPICS]. The next session is [DATE, TIME, TIME ZONE] at [LOCATION OR LINK]. [SPONSOR], if applicable, supports the session as [ROLE].

The discussion will use [CONFIDENTIALITY RULE]. There is no hard pitching, recording or unapproved photography. Members are expected to contribute practical experience and respect the participation rules.

If the topic is relevant, please reply by [DATE]. I can share the charter and participant profile before you decide. Invitations are personal, so substitutions require host approval.

Best,
[HOST NAME]
[ROLE]
[CONTACT]

Disclaimer: Adapt privacy, consent and event terms for your jurisdiction.

title: Confidentiality and Participation Statement
instructions: Select one attribution rule and explain it verbally at the beginning of each session.
content:
# [COMMUNITY NAME] Confidentiality and Participation Statement

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]

This session is intended to support candid professional discussion. Participants may [USE INFORMATION WITHOUT ATTRIBUTION / NOT SHARE SESSION CONTENT] according to the rule stated by the host.

Participants must not identify a speaker, organization or other participant without permission. Recording, transcription, screenshots and photography are prohibited unless the host and affected participants approve them in advance.

Participants remain responsible for what they disclose. Do not share privileged, regulated, personal, security-sensitive or competitively sensitive information that you are not authorized to disclose. The organizer cannot promise legal privilege or absolute confidentiality.

Participants agree to contribute respectfully, avoid hard pitching, disclose relevant conflicts and request consent before follow-up contact or introductions.

Concerns should be reported privately to [CONTACT]. Breaches may result in warning, suspension or removal under [PROCESS].

Acknowledged by: [NAME]
Date: [DATE]

Disclaimer: This statement is not legal advice. Obtain qualified review for your format and jurisdiction.

title: Executive Community Sponsor Agreement Framework
instructions: Use this as a commercial discussion framework and have the final agreement reviewed professionally.
content:
# Sponsor Agreement Framework

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Parties: [COMMUNITY] and [SPONSOR]
Term: [START] to [END]

## Purpose and support
[SPONSOR] will provide [FUNDING OR IN-KIND SUPPORT] for [PROGRAM]. The relationship will be disclosed as [WORDING].

## Sponsor rights
The sponsor may [BRANDING, HOSTING, APPROVED PARTICIPATION, CONTENT RIGHTS]. Any stage time or demonstration must be labeled and approved in advance.

## Boundaries
The sponsor will not receive attendee lists, guaranteed meetings, private peer discussions or unrestricted follow-up rights. Introductions require a relevant reason and consent. The sponsor may not use confidential discussion as sales intelligence.

## Editorial independence
[COMMUNITY] controls invitations, facilitation, methodology and editorial conclusions. Sponsor input and funding will be disclosed where material.

## Data
Each party will process personal information only for agreed purposes under [PRIVACY TERMS].

## Conduct, review and termination
Concerns are escalated to [CONTACTS]. Renewal considers delivery, member relevance, consent-compliant follow-up and host behavior. Material boundary breaches may end the agreement under [PROCESS].

Disclaimer: This framework is not a contract or legal advice.

title: Sponsor Host Briefing
instructions: Brief every sponsor attendee, including senior leaders who join late.
content:
# [PROGRAM] Sponsor Host Briefing

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Sponsor: [SPONSOR]
Community lead: [NAME]

## Member promise
The session exists for [MEMBER PROFILE] to discuss [QUESTION]. Sponsor success depends on relevant contribution and trusted relationships, not immediate lead capture.

## You may
Welcome participants; explain your disclosed support; contribute concise operating experience; answer invited questions; request consent for relevant follow-up.

## You may not
Deliver an unapproved pitch; collect attendee data; force demonstrations; dominate discussion; promise community endorsement; make unrequested sales contact; quote participants.

## Opening
Use this wording: ‘[SPONSOR] supports this session. [COMMUNITY] controls invitations and facilitation. We are here to listen and contribute.’

## Escalation
Direct member-fit, confidentiality, press and data questions to [COMMUNITY LEAD]. Report any concern immediately.

Sponsor attendees: [NAMES]
Briefing acknowledged: [NAME / DATE]

Disclaimer: Adapt this briefing to the signed sponsor terms.

title: Executive Community Host Briefing
instructions: Use this before each session and document local adaptations.
content:
# [COMMUNITY NAME] Host Briefing

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Host: [NAME]
Session: [DATE / FORMAT]

## Before
Confirm why each participant belongs; review conflicts and accessibility needs; brief sponsors; prepare the opening question; confirm confidentiality, recording and photography rules; plan seating or contribution order.

## Open
State the purpose, participant profile, confidentiality rule, sponsor relationship and close. Keep introductions relevant and short.

## Facilitate
Invite experience before advice; ask dominant speakers to pause; include quieter perspectives without forcing disclosure; stop hard pitching; prevent unsafe or unnecessary detail; keep time.

## Close
Summarize decisions without attribution; ask for useful requests; explain introduction consent and feedback; confirm what will be shared.

## After
Complete follow-up by [DATE]; record only necessary data; escalate conduct or privacy concerns to [CONTACT]; note what should continue, change or stop.

Disclaimer: This is an operating checklist, not legal advice.

title: Executive Community Speaker Briefing
instructions: Send this before accepting slides or announcing the speaker.
content:
# [PROGRAM] Speaker Briefing

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Speaker: [NAME]
Host: [NAME]

## Audience and purpose
Participants are [PROFILE]. The session should help them [DECISION OR OUTCOME]. Assume executive context and avoid a basic company presentation.

## Format
You have [TIME] for opening context followed by [TIME] of facilitated discussion. Slides are [ALLOWED / NOT USED] and due [DATE].

## Content standards
Use practical examples; identify assumptions; disclose commercial interests; source external statistics; distinguish experience from universal guidance; avoid unsupported superlatives.

## Boundaries
No hard pitch, surprise demonstration, attendee-list request, unapproved recording or quotation of participants. [CONFIDENTIALITY RULE] applies.

## Accessibility
Provide readable materials, describe meaningful visuals and avoid relying on color alone.

## Follow-up
Approved resources: [LIST]. Participant follow-up requires consent.

Acknowledged: [NAME / DATE]

Disclaimer: Speakers remain responsible for their claims and permissions.

title: Executive Dinner Run of Show
instructions: Adapt timing to service, guest count and the discussion rule.
content:
# [DINNER NAME] Run of Show

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Host: [NAME]
Venue: [VENUE]
Topic: [DECISION QUESTION]

T-30: Confirm room, place cards, accessibility, dietary needs, service timing and sponsor boundaries.

0–20: Welcome guests individually. Avoid uncontrolled pitching during arrival.

20–30: Seat guests. State purpose, confidentiality rule, sponsor relationship, recording policy and timing.

30–45: Concise introductions: name, role and one relevant question.

45–95: Facilitated discussion. Use prepared prompts, balance contribution and stop selling.

95–110: Ask for implications, resources and consent-based introduction requests.

110–120: Close. Explain feedback, follow-up and what will not be published.

After: Send promised resources, confirm introductions with both parties, log incidents and complete the post-event review.

Disclaimer: Venue, privacy and hospitality obligations require local review.

title: Executive Roundtable Run of Show
instructions: Use one decision question and protect equal contribution.
content:
# [ROUNDTABLE NAME] Run of Show

Version: 1.1.0
Review date: [DATE]
Duration: [MINUTES]
Facilitator: [NAME]

0–10: Welcome, purpose, participant profile, confidentiality rule and sponsor disclosure.

10–20: Introductions. Each participant states role and one constraint connected to the topic.

20–30: Frame [DECISION QUESTION]. Present only the facts needed for discussion.

30–65: First round. Each participant shares experience or a question.

65–80: Facilitated comparison of decisions, tradeoffs and unresolved issues.

80–90: Practical close. Capture requested resources, consent-based introductions and one action each participant may take.

Facilitator prompts: What changed your decision? Which assumption matters most? What would make this fail? Which experience does not transfer?

After: Send non-attributed synthesis only if agreed. Do not send participant data to sponsors without consent.

Disclaimer: This template does not create legal privilege or confidentiality by itself.
